reference.title: Cable Reverse Grip Pulldown
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you pull the bar down to the chest, inhale as it rises.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short squeeze, about 2 s up

prescription.tempo: About 1.2 s down, brief squeeze at the chest, 2 s up
prescription.progression: Cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set; add load in small steps, then progress toward chin-ups.

cues.text: Sit tall on the seat under the pulley, feet flat; take the bar underhand, hands about shoulder width, arms long overhead.
Breathe out, draw the shoulder blades down and drive the elbows down to your sides, leaning back slightly; bring the bar to the upper chest.
Brief squeeze with the chest up and the elbows tucked.
Breathe in and let the bar rise under control until the arms are long.
Let the shoulder blades rise for a full stretch, then start the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning far back and rowing the bar down
mistakes.fix: Keep the lean small (about 10-15 degrees); the elbows do the work.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling with the arms only, shoulders shrugged up
mistakes.fix: Start each rep by drawing the shoulder blades down.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the bar crash up at the top
mistakes.fix: Control the return over about 2 seconds.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the bar behind the head or down to the belly
mistakes.fix: Bring it in front of the face to the upper chest.

kinematics.setup: Underhand, 44 cm between the hands on a 120 cm lat bar (shoulders 40 cm apart)

kinematics.norm: From nearly straight overhead to well bent with the bar at the upper chest (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: ≈159° between the upper arm and the trunk (overhead)
kinematics.peak: ≈35°, elbows -5.2 cm in front of the shoulder joints
kinematics.norm: From full overhead reach to the elbows at the sides, a little in front of the trunk (clinical opinion)
A small backward lean of about 10-20 degrees is common; large swings add momentum (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s down, 0.4 s at the chest, 2 s up
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #14647, Cable Reverse Grip Pulldown, video (movement reference)
Lusk, Hale and Russell 2010, grip width and forearm orientation effects on muscle activity during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 24(7):1895-1900)

Signorile, Zink and Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the shoulder or elbow, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull without swinging the trunk.
Keep the head out of the cable's path; the bar passes in front of the face.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow or wrist discomfort with the underhand grip: a neutral-grip handle or a slightly wider grip.
Shoulder discomfort overhead: stop the bar a little short of full reach at the top.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Main mover: pulls the upper arm down from overhead. Supinated pulldown grips gave somewhat lower latissimus activity than pronated grips in EMG comparisons (Lusk 2010; Signorile 2002), but still a large share; fully stretched at the top.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Main mover: pulls the upper arm down from overhead. Supinated pulldown grips gave somewhat lower latissimus activity than pronated grips in EMG comparisons (Lusk 2010; Signorile 2002), but still a large share; fully stretched at the top.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: The underhand grip puts the biceps in its strongest position as the elbows bend (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: The underhand grip puts the biceps in its strongest position as the elbows bend (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Draw the shoulder blades down and together at the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Draw the shoulder blades down and together at the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Assists shoulder extension as the elbows pass the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Assists shoulder extension as the elbows pass the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down while the trunk leans back a little (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the slight backward lean steady (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the slight backward lean steady (clinical opinion).
